subject.title: Durable core PR2/6: add optional shared-state foundation

question: Should OpenClaw core own this new shared residual durable-state schema and shared-database lease contract, or should cross-owner recovery facts remain with existing owner-specific stores and APIs?
rationale: The patch intentionally avoids inactive public configuration and has focused evidence, but deciding whether a generic cross-owner persistence layer belongs in core is a durable architecture and ownership choice rather than a mechanical code correction.

options.title: Pause behind the RFC decision
options.body: Keep this implementation unmerged until maintainers explicitly accept, narrow, or reject the residual durable boundary described by the related RFC.

options.title: Sponsor the residual boundary
options.body: Accept the shared durable-state direction and continue review with named state-owner reviewers responsible for its schema and lifecycle contract.

options.title: Reject shared durable state
options.body: Close this implementation direction and require remaining recovery or handoff gaps to be represented through existing owner-specific stores.

recommendation.title: Pause behind the RFC decision
recommendation.body: Keep this implementation unmerged until maintainers explicitly accept, narrow, or reject the residual durable boundary described by the related RFC.

likelyOwner.reason: The proposal-series author can supply the ownership analysis and narrow the patch in response to the maintainer direction; final acceptance remains a maintainer decision.
